tldr: xRouter is a toolcalling-based routing system trained end-to-end with reinforcement learning that balances cost and performance by learning when to answer directly or delegate to external models, eliminating hand-engineered routing rules.
contributions: A cost-aware reinforcement learning framework for multi-model LLM orchestration
An explicit cost-performance reward function (R_final = R_binary × (K - λC)) that gates reward on task success while penalizing cost
An open implementation covering the full RL training and evaluation pipeline
Empirical insights into learned routing behavior across diverse benchmarks
methods: The router (a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) observes queries and decides whether to answer directly or invoke external models via tool calls. It is trained using the DAPO (GRPO-style) algorithm with a success-gated, cost-aware reward. Training data comes from the Reasoning360 benchmark stratified by difficulty (easy/medium/hard) and augmented with simple queries. A model pool of 13 models across capability tiers (e.g., GPT-5, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-OSS series) is available for offloading. Cost accounting tracks per-turn and per-episode spend, normalized by a configurable per-turn cap.
results: xRouter achieves 80-90% of GPT-5's accuracy while consuming less than one-fifth of the cost on GPQA. The moderate cost penalty setting (λ=2) yielded the most balanced cost-performance trade-off across benchmarks. xRouter-7B variants maintained strong results across AIME25 and LiveBench without retraining, demonstrating generalization. Higher expenditure did not necessarily improve performance, and extreme λ values imposed overly rigid constraints that reduced accuracy.
limitations: Small open models struggle to elicit sophisticated orchestration behaviors
The non-monotonic relationship between λ and performance makes tuning sensitive
Fan-out and call depth are deliberately limited to control latency and cost, potentially restricting complex multi-model coordination
The router's cost utility can appear lower than cheap open-source models because those models have significantly lower API prices, even if they achieve lower overall accuracy
